record.paper_title: Twin-Field Quantum Key Distribution: Protocols, Security, and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can twin-field quantum key distribution be integrated with quantum memories and repeater-based architectures so that communication performance goes beyond the fundamental O(√η) scaling of repeaterless TF-QKD while remaining compatible with TF-QKD infrastructure? More specifically, what long-coherence, high-fidelity quantum memories, temporal-storage and synchronization mechanisms, and purification protocols are required to support hybrid designs that combine TF-QKD backbone links with entanglement-swapping repeaters for continental-scale quantum communication?

evidence.quote: Scaling TF-QKD beyond the fundamental O(√η) limit necessitates integration with quantum memories and repeater-based architectures.
Quantum memories enable temporal storage and synchronization, thereby improving throughput and error correction capabilities.
Furthermore, hybrid designs that combine TF-QKD backbone links with entanglement-swapping repeaters present opportunities for continental-scale communication.
Achieving this vision requires the development of long-coherence, high-fidelity quantum memories, as well as purification protocols that are compatible with TF-QKD infrastructure.

artifact.category_tag: Quantum key distribution and quantum repeaters
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. In point-to-point quantum key distribution (QKD) over a lossy optical channel of transmittance $\eta$, the secret-key capacity of any repeaterless protocol is upper bounded by the PLOB bound, which scales as $O(\eta)$ in the high-loss regime. Twin-field QKD (TF-QKD) is a measurement-device-independent protocol in which two distant parties (Alice and Bob) each send dim phase-randomized optical pulses to an untrusted central node (Charlie) that performs single-photon interference; the resulting secret-key rate scales as $O(\sqrt{\eta})$, beating the repeaterless bound while still using no quantum memory. A quantum repeater architecture inserts intermediate nodes equipped with quantum memories (systems capable of storing a qubit with coherence time $T_2$ and storage fidelity $F$) and performs entanglement swapping and entanglement purification between elementary links to achieve a key-rate scaling that is polynomial (rather than exponential) in the total distance.

Problem. Design a hybrid quantum communication architecture that integrates TF-QKD with memory-assisted, repeater-based entanglement distribution, and rigorously establish the following:

(a) Specify a protocol that uses TF-QKD-style single-photon interference at untrusted middle stations on each elementary segment of length $L_0$, combined with quantum memories at repeater nodes that store heralded states until adjacent segments succeed, followed by entanglement swapping and (optionally) entanglement purification, such that the asymptotic secret-key rate $R(L)$ over total distance $L = nL_0$ satisfies
$$R(L) = \omega(\sqrt{\eta_{\text{tot}}}) \quad \text{as } \eta_{\text{tot}} = e^{-L/L_{\text{att}}} \to 0,$$
i.e., strictly outperforms the $O(\sqrt{\eta_{\text{tot}}})$ scaling of repeaterless TF-QKD.

(b) Determine the minimal memory requirements (coherence time $T_2$, storage-and-retrieval efficiency $\eta_m$, and storage fidelity $F$) as functions of $L$, $L_0$, the elementary link success probability $p_0$, and the repetition rate $r$, that are sufficient for the protocol of (a) to yield a positive secret-key rate exceeding the PLOB bound at continental scales (e.g. $L \gtrsim 1000$ km).

(c) Provide a purification protocol compatible with the phase-encoded states produced by TF-QKD interference (i.e., acting on the heralded coherent/single-photon superposition states used in TF-QKD), and prove a threshold theorem giving the minimum elementary-link fidelity above which iterated purification plus entanglement swapping yields end-to-end fidelity bounded below by a target $F^* \in (1/2, 1)$ at distance $L$.

(d) Show synchronization and temporal-mode-matching conditions on the memories (e.g. timing jitter, indistinguishability of retrieved photons) under which the central interference visibility needed for TF-QKD security is preserved when one or both arms are stored and retrieved from memory.

A complete solution consists of an explicit protocol, security proof against collective (and ideally coherent) attacks, and quantitative thresholds for $(T_2, \eta_m, F, p_0, r)$ achieving the scaling and fidelity claims above.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a forward-looking open research direction: combining TF-QKD with quantum memories and repeaters to surpass the $O(\sqrt{\eta})$ scaling. While memory-assisted MDI-QKD and various repeater proposals have been studied, no full hybrid TF-QKD + repeater architecture with matching security proof, purification protocol, and demonstrated super-$\sqrt{\eta}$ continental-scale rate has been established; the problem is regarded as open in the QKD/quantum-repeater literature as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Twin-Field Quantum Key Distribution: Protocols, Security, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Scaling TF-QKD beyond the fundamental O(sqrt(eta)) limit necessitates integration with quantum memories and repeater-based architectures.
status_evidence.claim: The integration is identified as an outstanding open challenge requiring new memories and purification protocols.
